title: RAW UNREVIEWED: steeped tricoccum water transfers a plant claim to a scorpion recipient
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In Pliny XXII.29, the tricoccum passage says a scorpion covered by the plant, or sprinkled with water in which it has been steeped, is said to die immediately. Preserve the processing chain plant→steeped water→animal recipient→reported result and the direct-cover alternative as two routes to the same endpoint; do not treat the water as another plant part or as a human dose.

design.mechanism: The same plant material reaches the named animal recipient in two distinct forms: direct covering with the plant, or a prior steeping operation that yields water then sprinkled on the scorpion. The reported endpoint is invariant (immediate death); preserve operation order and the liquid's derived-material status, not a generic internal/external or plant-part list. The circle-tracing claim is a separate immobilization result and must not be merged with this lethal pair.
